subject: botany
question_text: Explain the scope of Botany taking plant physiology as an example.

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The book's answer opens directly with the mineral point; the one-line introduction of plant physiology is added here as standard answer-writing practice. The 1+1+2 split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Plant physiology introduced
lines: Plant physiology is the branch of Botany
that studies the functions and life
processes of plants, such as nutrition
steps.why: The question uses one branch as the example of Botany's scope, so the answer opens by stating what that branch is before listing its uses.
common_mistakes: Starting directly with fertilizers — say what plant physiology is first.
steps.memory_tip: Morphology = parts; physiology = processes. This question is about processes.
steps.margin_note: One sentence naming the branch and what it studies.

steps.label: Mineral nutrition
lines: Knowledge of the role of minerals in plant
nutrition helps in the rational use of
chemical fertilizers and in the control of
steps.why: Knowing which mineral does what lets a farmer add fertilizer only where it is needed and correct a deficiency once it is recognised.
common_mistakes: Writing 'fertilizers increase yield' alone — the marked idea is rational (correct, measured) use.
Dropping deficiency control — this point has two halves.
steps.memory_tip: One mineral point, two halves: use fertilizer correctly, correct deficiencies.

steps.label: Plant hormone applications

lines.text: Knowledge of plant hormones is useful in:
c) increasing the shelf life of leafy
e) rooting of stem cuttings for vegetative
Plant physiology guides fertilizer use and hormone applications in crops.

steps.why: Each hormone application is a real farm or garden practice; listing all five shows the scope the question asks for.
common_mistakes: Writing only two or three uses — the list has five and the two marks expect most of them.
Naming hormones (auxin, ethylene) without their uses — the uses are what is marked here.
steps.memory_tip: Five hormone uses in order: weeds, dormancy, shelf life, ripening, rooting.
steps.margin_note: The lettered list a) to e) carries two marks; keep every item.

insider_note: The five-part hormone list is the weight of this answer — a complete a) to e) list with the mineral point before it reads as a full 4-mark script.
